title: Duplicate peer-supplied download transfer tokens can orphan an active F-connection transfer session
rerun_result: 1 unittest OK per lane across 3.3.10, 3.3.x, master
source_invariant: active_users is keyed by username+token; activation overwrites same key; deactivation deletes by username+token without transfer-object identity; F-init/progress/close lookups depend on that active map
public_overlap: no exact direct public match captured in rev0035 targeted searches; transfer-lifecycle adjacent issues exist
impact_boundary: remote peer availability / transfer-session integrity; not RCE and not file disclosure by itself
fix_shape: guard duplicate activation or allocate local generation; identity-check deactivation/timeouts; bind file callbacks to the expected transfer/session object
compatibility_risk: low to moderate; fix can be local to transfer-token/session lifecycle if it preserves legitimate retry/requeue flows
decision: retain strict report-candidate; make next production-draft target; still not production-ready text

public_overlap: no exact direct public match captured in rev0035 targeted searches; protocol docs make compatibility constraints explicit
impact_boundary: remote peer connection-integrity / routing confusion; higher architectural impact than U-123 but more compatibility-sensitive

compatibility_risk: high; naive rejection can break legitimate direct/indirect races and fallback behavior
